# banditlab

banditlab is an R framework for multi-armed bandit experimentation:
simulating, comparing and extending sequential decision algorithms.

It provides:

- **Environments**: Bernoulli, Gaussian, and arbitrary user-defined
  reward processes.
- **Policies**: random, greedy (with optimistic initial values),
  epsilon-greedy (fixed and scheduled), explore-then-commit, UCB1 and
  Beta-Bernoulli Thompson sampling.
- **One experiment engine**: replicated runs, one independent random
  number stream per replicate (results do not depend on how many
  replicates you run), and seed-paired policy comparisons by
  construction.
- **Explicit metrics**: pseudo-regret with exact documented definitions
  ([`?regret_definitions`](https://rprodigest.github.io/banditlab/reference/regret_definitions.md)),
  never computed when the environment cannot support them.
- **Tidy results**: summaries, checkpoints and full trajectories as
  tibbles, sized deliberately (trajectories are opt-in).
- **Propensity-complete logs**: every built-in stochastic policy logs
  the marginal probability of each selected action, the prerequisite for
  importance-weighted offline evaluation.
- **A small extension API**: implement three S3 methods and your policy
  runs in the same engine as the built-ins
  ([`vignette("custom-policies")`](https://rprodigest.github.io/banditlab/articles/custom-policies.md)).

## Why it exists

The only general bandit framework R has had, `contextual`, was archived
from CRAN in 2021. What remains covers Bayesian A/B analysis and
clinical trial designs, not general bandit experimentation. banditlab
fills that gap with a deliberately small, tested, dependency-light core
(tibble and ggplot2 are the only non-base imports).

## Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

``` r

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("RProDigest/banditlab")
```

Once released on CRAN:

``` r

install.packages("banditlab")
```

## In 60 seconds

``` r

library(banditlab)

env <- bandit_bernoulli(c(low = 0.15, mid = 0.25, high = 0.40))

result <- run_experiment(
  env,
  policies = list(
    epsilon  = policy_epsilon_greedy(0.1),
    ucb      = policy_ucb1(),
    thompson = policy_thompson()
  ),
  horizon = 1000,
  replications = 50,
  seed = 42,
  checkpoints = seq(50, 1000, by = 50)
)

summary(result)
#> one row per policy: mean and quantiles of final cumulative regret,
#> mean reward, mean optimal-action share

autoplot(result, metric = "cumulative_regret")
```

Seed-paired comparison against a baseline:

``` r

cmp <- compare_policies(result, baseline = "epsilon")
aggregate(difference ~ policy, data = cmp, FUN = mean)
```

## Telecoms case study

The article [Bandits for RAN optimisation: 5G NR link
adaptation](https://rprodigest.github.io/banditlab/articles/nr-link-adaptation.html)
uses banditlab to compare bandit policies with a static CQI rule and
outer-loop link adaptation (OLLA) in simulated stationary and drifting
radio conditions. It builds both industry baselines with the extension
API, without modifying the package.

## Extending

A custom policy is a constructor plus three S3 methods
([`policy_state()`](https://rprodigest.github.io/banditlab/reference/policy_interface.md),
[`select_arm()`](https://rprodigest.github.io/banditlab/reference/policy_interface.md),
[`update_state()`](https://rprodigest.github.io/banditlab/reference/policy_interface.md)).
The vignette
[`vignette("custom-policies")`](https://rprodigest.github.io/banditlab/articles/custom-policies.md)
implements softmax exploration from scratch and runs it against the
built-in policies; the package’s own test suite runs a policy
implemented this way to guarantee the extension interface keeps working.

## Relationship to the book

banditlab is the computational companion of the book in progress
*Adaptive Bandit Methods with R*, which teaches the algorithms by
building transparent implementations before introducing the package. The
package is designed to stand alone: nothing in its documentation
requires the book.

## Development status

Version 0.1.0. The public API described in the reference and vignettes
is intended to be stable; the extension generics
([`policy_state()`](https://rprodigest.github.io/banditlab/reference/policy_interface.md),
[`select_arm()`](https://rprodigest.github.io/banditlab/reference/policy_interface.md),
[`update_state()`](https://rprodigest.github.io/banditlab/reference/policy_interface.md))
are the package’s compatibility contract. Planned directions
(non-stationary environments, contextual policies, offline evaluation)
are listed in the repository’s roadmap.

## License

MIT.

# Package index

## All functions

- [`as_tibble(`*`<bandit_result>`*`)`](https://rprodigest.github.io/banditlab/reference/as_tibble.bandit_result.md)
  : Convert experiment results to a tibble
- [`autoplot(`*`<bandit_result>`*`)`](https://rprodigest.github.io/banditlab/reference/autoplot.bandit_result.md)
  : Plot bandit experiment results
- [`bandit_bernoulli()`](https://rprodigest.github.io/banditlab/reference/bandit_bernoulli.md)
  : Create a Bernoulli bandit environment
- [`bandit_custom()`](https://rprodigest.github.io/banditlab/reference/bandit_custom.md)
  : Create a custom bandit environment
- [`bandit_gaussian()`](https://rprodigest.github.io/banditlab/reference/bandit_gaussian.md)
  : Create a Gaussian bandit environment
- [`compare_policies()`](https://rprodigest.github.io/banditlab/reference/compare_policies.md)
  : Seed-paired policy comparison
- [`policy_epsilon_greedy()`](https://rprodigest.github.io/banditlab/reference/policy_epsilon_greedy.md)
  : Epsilon-greedy policy
- [`policy_etc()`](https://rprodigest.github.io/banditlab/reference/policy_etc.md)
  : Explore-then-commit policy
- [`policy_greedy()`](https://rprodigest.github.io/banditlab/reference/policy_greedy.md)
  : Greedy policy with optional optimistic initial values
- [`policy_state()`](https://rprodigest.github.io/banditlab/reference/policy_interface.md)
  [`select_arm()`](https://rprodigest.github.io/banditlab/reference/policy_interface.md)
  [`update_state()`](https://rprodigest.github.io/banditlab/reference/policy_interface.md)
  : The policy extension interface
- [`policy_random()`](https://rprodigest.github.io/banditlab/reference/policy_random.md)
  : Random selection policy
- [`policy_thompson()`](https://rprodigest.github.io/banditlab/reference/policy_thompson.md)
  : Beta-Bernoulli Thompson sampling policy
- [`policy_ucb1()`](https://rprodigest.github.io/banditlab/reference/policy_ucb1.md)
  : UCB1 policy
- [`regret_definitions`](https://rprodigest.github.io/banditlab/reference/regret_definitions.md)
  : Regret definitions used by banditlab
- [`run_experiment()`](https://rprodigest.github.io/banditlab/reference/run_experiment.md)
  : Run a replicated bandit experiment
- [`sample_reward()`](https://rprodigest.github.io/banditlab/reference/sample_reward.md)
  : Draw one reward from an environment
- [`scale_colour_banditlab()`](https://rprodigest.github.io/banditlab/reference/scale_colour_banditlab.md)
  [`scale_fill_banditlab()`](https://rprodigest.github.io/banditlab/reference/scale_colour_banditlab.md)
  [`scale_color_banditlab()`](https://rprodigest.github.io/banditlab/reference/scale_colour_banditlab.md)
  : Okabe-Ito-based discrete colour and fill scales
- [`summary(`*`<bandit_result>`*`)`](https://rprodigest.github.io/banditlab/reference/summary.bandit_result.md)
  : Summarise a bandit experiment
- [`theme_banditlab()`](https://rprodigest.github.io/banditlab/reference/theme_banditlab.md)
  : banditlab plot theme
